wisdom.content: Durable-mutation success is gated on Temporal durability only, NOT disk durability. adv_delta_add (and the shared signal+readback family: gates.ts, spec-deltas.ts, wisdom.ts, tasks.ts, changes.ts) returns success after fireSignalWithMutationGuard confirms signal-in-history + reducer-applied via changeStateQuery readback — but then calls persistStateToDisk WITHOUT await (store-temporal/index.ts:219-250: `void (async()=>{...})()`, failure swallowed at debug). The disk projection is the SOLE source of truth once a workflow orphans (dead session queue), yet it's written fire-and-forget + swallow-on-failure. So success:true can be returned, the session can exit before the async changes.save flushes (or it fails silently), and the mutation becomes invisible to every disk-first reader (adv_delta_list/show, adv_change_show fallback) with no error. Durability model is inverted: the layer that must survive orphaning is written weakest. Not "signal-accept without persistence" — Temporal IS confirmed — but "confirmed Temporal persistence with unconfirmed best-effort disk persistence." Fix tracked in change gateMutationSuccessDisk (Epic hardenTemporalReliability entry 14): gate durable-mutation success on disk-projection durability (await + classify disk write, or invert to disk-authoritative writes). Sibling of rq-releaseProjectionDurability01 (read/terminal side) and Epic shell entry 6.

Discovery (code-verified) — the disk-durability seam has a BROADER blast radius than the base fire-and-forget write. (1) Reducer dedup is correct (change-state.ts:1732-1768: applySpecDeltaAddedToState scans ALL capabilities and throws on duplicate delta.id). So the peer's improveCrossProject duplicate-ID acceptance (dl-q7m2Kp9xR4vB accepted twice) PROVES the authoritative workflow state did NOT retain delta#1 by request #2 — not merely a stale disk read. (2) Continue-as-new seed DOES include `deltas: state.deltas` (workflows.ts:1933), so CAN preserves deltas in the happy path — not the culprit. (3) Unifying mechanism: reseedChangeFromDisk (index.ts:585) reseeds with getCurrentSessionId (:636). If session A's unawaited fire-and-forget disk write hasn't flushed when session B reseeds an orphaned workflow, the rebuilt workflow LACKS delta#1 → duplicate add accepted → invisible with no error. The disk projection is BOTH the reseed source AND the weakest-guaranteed write. (4) reseedChangeFromDisk is GATED OUT on query_failed classification (index.ts:828-830) — a timing-out orphaned workflow cannot self-heal via reseed; disk-first reads bypass Temporal so they never trigger catch→reseed, and the signal path throws on SC4. (5) Live dogfooding this change: its own workflow orphaned on a dead prior-session queue; disk reads worked (40ms) while every Temporal query/signal timed out; OpenCode restart + OrphanQueueAdopter (10s heartbeat, FIFO) recovered it — confirming orphan-queue, not poisoned. Design implication: disk-first reads are the reliable layer under Temporal wedge → favors Direction 2 (disk-authoritative). SC4 tension: Direction 2 lets a mutation succeed on disk while the workflow is orphaned, which RELOCATES (not weakens) SC4's no-false-success guarantee from Temporal-readback to disk-fsync. Needs user steer.

FOLLOW-UP for Epic entry 6 (disk-authoritative reads/writes): concurrent-session projection serialization. Design validator (adv-researcher, 2026-07-23) found that await-own-write (this change, Direction 1) does NOT close two concurrent races: (#1 reseed-during-window) a peer session reseedChangeFromDisk-es from stale disk during another session's in-flight mutation; (#2 stale-overwrite) two sessions write the whole change.json from different readbacks — atomic rename prevents torn files but not stale last-writer-wins, so the disk projection can REGRESS even though the Temporal workflow stays monotonic. This is the concurrent-session generalization of the peer improveCrossProject duplicate-ID acceptance bug. Robust fix needs a monotonic generation or per-change cross-process lease/CAS. BLOCKER for a cheap in-place fix: change state has NO general per-mutation monotonic revision — acceptanceReadinessRevision advances only on acceptance-affecting mutations; Temporal historyLength resets at continue-as-new; lastSignalAt is a timestamp (equal-ms tie hole, P33). A proper fix must add a monotonic projectionRevision to the reducer + CAN seed + replay-determinism harness (the exact replay-sensitive surface that has repeatedly poisoned this Epic — treat with replay-determinism gating). User-approved Option A (2026-07-23): ship single-writer honesty here, defer concurrent-writer durability to entry 6. When entry 6 is planned: (a) add monotonic projectionRevision; (b) CAS-guard whole-file projection writes (write iff incoming >= on-disk generation); (c) make reseedChangeFromDisk participate in the same cross-process protocol so it never adopts a snapshot older than the workflow's known generation.

For durability seams, a pure outcome-gate unit test (e.g. assertDurablePersist) is necessary but NOT sufficient: every durability-critical PUBLIC mutation path must have its own regression test proving that a post-ack disk-write failure rejects with the typed error (DiskProjectionPersistError) rather than returning success. Rationale (harden reviewer, gateMutationSuccessDisk): each caller independently awaits the durable helper; a future edit can silently restore success-before-disk-durability on one path while the pure-gate test + other paths stay green. Coverage added per path: spec-deltas.add, gates.complete, gates.reopenFrom, wisdom.add, tasks.update/add/cancel/reclassifyTdd — each asserts (a) persist called with confirmed post-signal state and (b) rejection propagates on disk failure. Pattern: mock ./shared (runTemporal/runTemporalQuery/getGuardedChangeHandle) + inject a rejecting persistStateToDiskDurable/persistAndRefreshDurable.

items.text: **AC1 (RED→GREEN, the concrete proof):** A durability-critical mutation whose disk write is (simulated) failing MUST NOT return `success:true` with the mutation absent from the disk projection. RED reproduces current behavior (`success:true` + mutation absent because the failure is swallowed); GREEN surfaces or degrades the failure so success never outruns disk durability.

**AC2 (success ⇒ own disk write durable):** For every durability-critical mutation, a `success:true` return guarantees the disk projection contains the mutation at return time, via an awaited+confirmed atomic disk write. (Durability against a *concurrent* session overwriting the projection afterward is Out of scope — see below.)

**AC3 (no-false-success preserved / SC4):** Under an orphaned or unreachable workflow, the no-false-success guarantee holds: the mutation throws at the SC4 signal guard before the disk write. No silent false success. SC4 semantics unchanged.

**AC4 (reads stay disk-first):** Reads (`adv_change_show`, `adv_gate_status`, `adv_delta_list/show`) remain disk-first and acquire NO hard Temporal dependency. (Dogfooded 2026-07-23: disk reads 40ms while the workflow was fully wedged.)

**AC5 (failures surfaced, not swallowed):** Disk-write failures on durability-critical mutations are classified and surfaced as a typed error, not swallowed at debug (`index.ts:229-250` current behavior).

**AC6 (explicit durability-critical set):** The durability-critical mutation set is explicitly enumerated (spec deltas, gate completions, wisdom, tasks) and distinguished from non-critical hot paths (e.g. cache-refresh dual-writes) that need not pay the stronger gate.

**AC7 (typed ambiguous outcome — validator-required):** When the Temporal signal is acknowledged (mutation applied in workflow history) but the subsequent disk write fails, the mutation MUST return a typed ambiguous/failed outcome — distinct from both success and a generic error — and MUST NOT advise blind retry, because Temporal may have durably applied the mutation despite the caller-visible failure. Mirrors the existing `outcome_unknown_readback_unavailable` handling.
No hard Temporal dependency on the read path (AC4).
Preserve append-only delta semantics; archive remains the sole global-spec writer.
Do not make disk-write latency block non-durability-critical hot paths unnecessarily (AC6 classification governs this).
Do NOT weaken the no-false-success guarantee (SC4). Relocating the guarantee to a confirmed disk-fsync under a disk-authoritative direction is a Direction-2 concern, not this change.
Do NOT resolve the concurrent-projection races by adding a hard Temporal read dependency.
Do NOT add a monotonic-generation/CAS field to the replay-sensitive workflow reducer in this change (replay-determinism risk); that belongs with the deferred concurrency-control work.

documents.proposal:
# Gate durable-mutation success on disk-projection durability

## Root Cause Analysis

**Defect (unintended behavior):** `adv_delta_add` (and every sibling mutation routed through the same signal→readback→persist pattern) returns `success:true` when the mutation is durable in **Temporal history + reducer-applied**, but the **disk projection write is not part of the success gate**. Since the disk projection is the *only* readable source of truth once a workflow orphans (dead session queue, poisoned history, unreachable worker), a mutation can be reported successful yet later be invisible to all disk-first readers.

**Tier-1 code evidence:**

- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/spec-deltas.ts:57-97` (`add`): fires `fireSignalWithMutationGuard`, throws on `outcome_unknown_readback_unavailable`, re-queries `changeStateQuery`, confirms the delta is present in `state.deltas[capability]`, then calls `persistStateToDisk(changeId, state)` **without `await`** (line 95) and returns. The same unawaited call appears in `modify` (135), `amend` (176), `retract` (216), `remove` (255), `rename` (295).
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/gates.ts:46-86` (`fireSignalWithMutationGuard`): the success gate is signal-dispatch + a single `query(changeStateQuery)` readback. `enforceMutationEligibilityForError` (line 63) correctly throws on SC4 classes (no-poller / unregistered-query / deadline / resource-exhaustion), so mutations against an orphaned workflow throw rather than falsely succeed. The guard proves **Temporal** durability only — it never touches disk.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:219-250` (`persistStateToDisk`): body is `void (async () => { try { await legacy.changes.save(mapped); } catch (err) { logger.debug(...); } })();` — **unawaited fire-and-forget, failure swallowed at debug.** Doc comment (lines 215-217): *"disk write is a durability fallback, not a correctness gate. Temporal remains the source of truth during the live session."*
- Same unawaited pattern in `gates.ts:177,212` and `wisdom.ts:56`.

**Why the stated assumption fails:** the code assumes *"Temporal is the source of truth during the live session."* The exact failure mode this Epic exists to fix is **session end** — the workflow orphans (see `autoAdoptOrphanSessionQueues` RCA: change workflows are pinned to ephemeral `advance-{projectId}-sess_{id}` queues via `workflow-start.ts:53`; session exit leaves the workflow unpolled). At that point Temporal is unreadable and disk is the only truth — but disk was written with the weakest guarantee: unawaited, unconfirmed, swallow-on-failure.

**Observed corroboration (this session):** the `dl-aDOptOrph01` delta on `autoAdoptOrphanSessionQueues` was readable via `adv_delta_list` (disk-first) but returned `deltas:{}` via `adv_change_show` (stale workflow-projection fallback, `_recovery: temporal_query_fallback / missing_workflow`). In that instance the async disk write had flushed, so the read mismatch was in `change_show`'s fallback path — but the same fire-and-forget seam is the more dangerous latent version: had the process exited before the async `changes.save` flushed, the delta would have been permanently invisible with no error.

## What Changes

For durability-critical mutations, `success:true` MUST mean durable in the layer that survives orphaning. Two candidate directions (to be resolved in design):

1. **Await disk into the success gate** — make `persistStateToDisk` awaited and classify its outcome for durability-critical mutations (spec deltas, gate completions, terminal transitions, wisdom). Disk-write failure fails/degrades the mutation rather than being swallowed. `success:true` ⇒ Temporal history **and** disk projection both durable.
2. **Invert per Epic invariant #1** — disk projection is the authoritative durable write (awaited, fsync-safe), Temporal signalled as accelerator afterward; success = disk confirmed.

Minimum bar (either direction): the fallback source of truth cannot be written with a weaker guarantee than the success return implies. Must remain safe under orphaned/unreachable workflows and must not reintroduce a hard Temporal dependency on the read path.

## Scope (initial, refine in discovery/design)

- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts` — `persistStateToDisk` durability semantics (await + failure classification).
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/spec-deltas.ts`, `gates.ts`, `wisdom.ts`, `tasks.ts`, `changes.ts` — success-gate wiring for durability-critical mutations.
- Tests proving: success ⇒ disk durable; disk-write failure surfaces (not swallowed); orphaned-workflow mutations still throw (no regression to the SC4 guard); read path never hard-depends on Temporal.

## Constraints / avoidances

- Do NOT reintroduce a hard Temporal dependency on reads.
- Do NOT make disk-write latency block non-durability-critical hot paths unnecessarily — classify which mutations need the stronger gate.
- Do NOT weaken the existing SC4 mutation-eligibility guard (orphaned-workflow mutations must still throw).
- Preserve append-only delta semantics; archive remains the sole global-spec writer.

## Relationship

Sibling of the `rq-releaseProjectionDurability01` false-negative family and Epic shell entry 6 (disk-authoritative reads). This change addresses the **write** side of the same invariant: durable mutations must make the disk projection durable before claiming success.

## Validation plan

- RED: mutation returns success while a simulated disk-write failure is swallowed (current behavior) → assert the mutation is absent from the disk projection despite success:true.
- GREEN: success is gated on (or fails/degrades with) disk durability; disk-write failure is surfaced, not swallowed.
- Regression: orphaned/unreachable workflow still throws at the mutation guard; read path degrades to disk without hard Temporal dependency.
documents.problemStatement: Durable-mutation tools (adv_delta_add and the shared signal+readback family — spec deltas, gate completion, task/wisdom/epic mutations) return success:true after confirming Temporal-history durability + reducer application, but BEFORE the disk projection — the artifact that becomes the sole source of truth once a workflow orphans — is durably written. The disk write (persistStateToDisk) is fire-and-forget (unawaited) and swallow-on-failure. A mutation can return success, the session can exit before the async disk write flushes (or it can fail silently), and the mutation is then invisible to every disk-first reader with no error ever surfaced. This inverts the durability model: the layer that must survive orphaning is written with the weakest guarantee.

# Agreement — Gate durable-mutation success on disk-projection durability

## Objective

Durable-mutation `success:true` MUST mean the mutation is durable in the layer that survives workflow orphaning — the **disk projection** — not merely in Temporal history. Eliminate the false-success class where a mutation returns `success:true` yet is absent from every disk-first reader with no error surfaced.

Scope is the **single-writer honesty** side of Epic invariant #1. Concurrent-session projection serialization is explicitly deferred (see Out of scope). Sibling of `rq-releaseProjectionDurability01` (read/terminal side).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (RED→GREEN, the concrete proof):** A durability-critical mutation whose disk write is (simulated) failing MUST NOT return `success:true` with the mutation absent from the disk projection. RED reproduces current behavior (`success:true` + mutation absent because the failure is swallowed); GREEN surfaces or degrades the failure so success never outruns disk durability.
- **AC2 (success ⇒ own disk write durable):** For every durability-critical mutation, a `success:true` return guarantees the disk projection contains the mutation at return time, via an awaited+confirmed atomic disk write. (Durability against a *concurrent* session overwriting the projection afterward is Out of scope — see below.)
- **AC3 (no-false-success preserved / SC4):** Under an orphaned or unreachable workflow, the no-false-success guarantee holds: the mutation throws at the SC4 signal guard before the disk write. No silent false success. SC4 semantics unchanged.
- **AC4 (reads stay disk-first):** Reads (`adv_change_show`, `adv_gate_status`, `adv_delta_list/show`) remain disk-first and acquire NO hard Temporal dependency. (Dogfooded 2026-07-23: disk reads 40ms while the workflow was fully wedged.)
- **AC5 (failures surfaced, not swallowed):** Disk-write failures on durability-critical mutations are classified and surfaced as a typed error, not swallowed at debug (`index.ts:229-250` current behavior).
- **AC6 (explicit durability-critical set):** The durability-critical mutation set is explicitly enumerated (spec deltas, gate completions, wisdom, tasks) and distinguished from non-critical hot paths (e.g. cache-refresh dual-writes) that need not pay the stronger gate.
- **AC7 (typed ambiguous outcome — validator-required):** When the Temporal signal is acknowledged (mutation applied in workflow history) but the subsequent disk write fails, the mutation MUST return a typed ambiguous/failed outcome — distinct from both success and a generic error — and MUST NOT advise blind retry, because Temporal may have durably applied the mutation despite the caller-visible failure. Mirrors the existing `outcome_unknown_readback_unavailable` handling.

## Constraints

- No hard Temporal dependency on the read path (AC4).
- Preserve append-only delta semantics; archive remains the sole global-spec writer.
- Do not make disk-write latency block non-durability-critical hot paths unnecessarily (AC6 classification governs this).

## Avoidances

- Do NOT weaken the no-false-success guarantee (SC4). Relocating the guarantee to a confirmed disk-fsync under a disk-authoritative direction is a Direction-2 concern, not this change.
- Do NOT resolve the concurrent-projection races by adding a hard Temporal read dependency.
- Do NOT add a monotonic-generation/CAS field to the replay-sensitive workflow reducer in this change (replay-determinism risk); that belongs with the deferred concurrency-control work.

## Out of scope (→ Epic entry 6: disk-authoritative reads/writes)

Concurrent-session projection serialization, per the design-validator CONFLICT resolution (user-approved Option A, 2026-07-23):

- **Race #1 (reseed-during-window):** a peer session `reseedChangeFromDisk`-es from a stale disk snapshot during another session's in-flight mutation.
- **Race #2 (stale-overwrite):** two sessions each write the whole `change.json` from different readbacks; atomic `rename` prevents torn files but not stale last-writer-wins, so the projection can regress even while the Temporal workflow stays monotonic.

Robustly closing these requires a monotonic generation or per-change cross-process lease/CAS that the change state does not currently carry. Deferred to the disk-authoritative Epic entry, which already owns the replacement concurrency control for Temporal's single-writer serialization. This change delivers single-writer honesty; it does not claim concurrent-writer durability.

# Design — Gate durable-mutation success on disk-projection durability

## Chosen direction

**Direction 1 — await disk into the success gate.** SC4 read literally: orphaned-workflow mutations still throw at the Temporal signal guard. Direction 2 (disk-authoritative inversion) and concurrent-projection serialization are deferred to Epic entry 6. User-approved 2026-07-23; design-validator CONFLICT resolved via user-approved Option A (scope concurrent races out).

## Durability model (the fix in one line)

Today: `success:true` ⇒ Temporal history durable + reducer-applied, disk write fire-and-forget/swallowed. Target: for durability-critical mutations, `success:true` ⇒ Temporal history durable **and** this session's atomic disk write completed (awaited + failure surfaced).

## Why awaited `writeFile` is sufficient (no fsync) — validator PASS-with-scope

`persistStateToDisk` → `legacy.changes.save` → `saveChange` (json.ts:582) → `atomicWriteFile` (jsonl-atomic-writer.ts:40-41): awaited `writeFile(tmp)` + atomic `rename(tmp, path)`. Already awaited + torn-write-safe; only `persistStateToDisk` fires it unawaited and swallows failure.

The defect's failure mode is **session/process exit before the async write flushes**. An awaited `fs/promises.writeFile` resolves after the write syscall completes; the data is in kernel page cache, which survives process exit — the OS flushes independently. `fsync`/`fdatasync` only adds **system-crash/power-loss** durability ([fsync(2)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html)), a strictly stronger property this change does not target.

Precise wording (per validator): the guarantee is **"sufficient against ordinary process/session exit on supported local POSIX filesystems; not crash-consistent storage durability."** Caveats explicitly noted, not fixed here: (a) full crash-safe rename persistence would also need to fsync the containing directory; (b) network filesystems (NFS) have distinct `rename(2)` failure ambiguity. Decision (P19/P29/P33): do not add fsync speculatively; await the existing atomic write.

## Architecture / LBP decisions

1. **`persistStateToDisk` returns a typed outcome.** `(changeId, state) => Promise<DiskPersistOutcome>` where `DiskPersistOutcome = { kind: "persisted" } | { kind: "skipped"; reason: "archived" } | { kind: "failed"; error: unknown }`. Archived-skip branch (index.ts:223-228) → `skipped`.
2. **Durability-critical callers await + throw a typed ambiguous error (AC7).** Helper `persistStateToDiskDurable(changeId, state)` awaits `persistStateToDisk` and, on `kind: "failed"`, throws a typed `DiskProjectionPersistError` that encodes the **ambiguous** semantics: the Temporal signal was already acknowledged (readback confirmed the mutation) but the disk projection did not persist — the mutation may be durable in Temporal; the caller must NOT blind-retry. This mirrors the existing `outcome_unknown_readback_unavailable` contract (spec-deltas.ts:73-77). `success:true` is never returned without a durable disk write (AC2, AC5).
3. **Non-durability-critical callers keep EXPLICIT fire-and-forget.** `voidPersist(changeId, state)` `void`s the promise + logs failure at debug — preserving today's latency for hot paths, but making the fire-and-forget choice explicit at the call site (AC6). No hot path silently inherits the stronger gate.
4. **Ordering, one await added:** signal → Temporal readback (durable) → **await disk (durable)** → return. Closes the single-actor retry case: after success, this session's disk has the mutation, so its own subsequent readers/reseeds see it.
5. **SC4 untouched.** `fireSignalWithMutationGuard` / `enforceMutationEligibilityForError` (gates.ts:46-86) unmodified. Orphaned/unreachable workflow throws at signal dispatch, before the disk write. AC3 by construction.
6. **Read path untouched.** No reader gains a Temporal dependency (validator PASS on claim 3). AC4 holds by not-touching.

## Concurrency boundary (validator CONFLICT resolution — scoped OUT to entry 6)

The design validator (adv-researcher, 2026-07-23) returned CONFLICT: await-own-write does not close two concurrent-session races —
- **Race #1 (reseed-during-window):** a peer session reseeds from stale disk during this session's in-flight mutation (between Temporal readback and disk-write completion). Narrow (~one atomic write) but real.
- **Race #2 (stale-overwrite):** two sessions write the whole `change.json` from different readbacks; atomic `rename` prevents torn files but not stale last-writer-wins → the projection can regress while the Temporal workflow stays monotonic.

**Why not fixed here:** a structurally-correct fix needs a monotonic generation or per-change cross-process lease/CAS. The change state carries **no** general per-mutation revision (`acceptanceReadinessRevision` advances only on acceptance-affecting mutations; Temporal `historyLength` resets at continue-as-new; `lastSignalAt` is a timestamp — using it for ordering is a P33 heuristic hole at equal-ms ties). Adding a monotonic `projectionRevision` to the reducer + CAN seed + replay-determinism is exactly the replay-sensitive surface that has repeatedly poisoned this Epic. **User-approved Option A:** defer concurrent-projection serialization to Epic entry 6 (disk-authoritative reads/writes), which already owns the replacement concurrency control. This change delivers single-writer honesty only.

## Deferral soundness (validator PASS-with-amendment)

Retaining Temporal as live-session serialization authority and rejecting critical mutations when Temporal is unavailable (SC4-throw, restart-to-recover) is a coherent, safe steady state — safer than silently accepting an unserializable mutation. The only required amendment (AC7) is the typed ambiguous outcome, incorporated in decision #2.

## Implementation strategy

1. Refactor `persistStateToDisk` (index.ts:219-250) to `async` returning `DiskPersistOutcome`; keep the archived-skip branch.
2. Add typed `DiskProjectionPersistError` (carries ambiguous semantics per AC7) + `persistStateToDiskDurable` (await+throw) + `voidPersist` (explicit fire-and-forget) helpers.
3. Rewire durability-critical callers from unawaited `persistStateToDisk(...)` to `await persistStateToDiskDurable(...)`.
4. Leave `dualWriteAfterMutation` (index.ts:268) and other non-critical callers on `voidPersist`.

## Durability-critical set (AC6)

Await+throw applied to: **spec-deltas** add/modify/amend/retract/remove/rename (spec-deltas.ts:95/135/176/216/255/295), **gate completion** (gates.ts:177/212), **wisdom.add** (wisdom.ts:56), **task** state mutations (tasks.ts). Archive keeps its own bundle path (skipped:archived). Non-critical: `dualWriteAfterMutation` cache-refresh (re-derives from a post-mutation query, never gates a caller's success) → `voidPersist`.

## RED test (concrete — AC1)

Inject a failing `legacy.changes.save` (mock throws) on a durability-critical mutation (spec-delta add or gate complete):
- **RED (current):** mutation returns `success:true` while the disk projection does NOT contain the mutation (failure swallowed at debug). Assert both: `success === true` AND disk projection missing the mutation.
- **GREEN (target):** mutation throws `DiskProjectionPersistError` (no `success:true`); disk-write failure surfaced with ambiguous semantics.

## Testing

- **AC1** RED→GREEN (anchor test).
- **AC2** success ⇒ disk projection contains the mutation (positive path, real temp-dir write).
- **AC3** regression: orphaned/unreachable-workflow mutation still throws at SC4 (existing SC4 tests green; add one asserting the disk write is never reached on SC4-throw).
- **AC4** read path has no hard Temporal dependency (read a change whose workflow is wedged → returns disk).
- **AC5** disk-write failure classified/surfaced (typed error), distinct from a swallowed debug log.
- **AC6** durability-critical set awaits+throws; `dualWriteAfterMutation` does not gate success on disk.
- **AC7** signal-acked-but-disk-failed → typed `DiskProjectionPersistError` with ambiguous/no-blind-retry semantics.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Latency:** one awaited atomic write per durability-critical mutation; bounded to the enumerated set; hot paths stay on `voidPersist`.
- **Partial rewire:** a missed durability-critical caller retains old swallow behavior. Mitigation: enumerate the set in one place; AC6 test asserts each wired caller throws on disk failure.
- **Concurrent-projection regression (races #1/#2):** knowingly out of scope (entry 6). This change does not claim concurrent-writer durability; the agreement states this explicitly.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Concurrent-projection serialization (races #1/#2) + monotonic generation/lease → Epic entry 6.
- Direction 2 disk-authoritative inversion → Epic entry 6.
- `fsync`/directory-fsync/power-loss durability; NFS rename ambiguity → separate hardening if ever required.
- Changes to the Temporal reducer, SC4 guard, or read-path fallback.

## Sources

- Node.js fs — https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/fs.html
- fsync(2) — https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html
- rename(2) — https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/rename.2.html
- Temporal message-passing — https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/message-passing

# Executive Summary — Gate durable-mutation success on disk-projection durability

## Outcome

Durable ADV mutations (spec deltas, gate completions, wisdom, task changes) now report `success` only when the change is durable in the layer that survives a workflow going dark — the on-disk projection — not merely in Temporal. Previously a mutation could return `success:true` while its disk write was fire-and-forget and its failure silently swallowed, so the change could vanish from every disk-first reader with no error. That false-success class is closed.

## Why it matters

The disk projection is the sole source of truth once a change's workflow orphans (a recurring failure this Epic targets). Writing that layer with the weakest guarantee — while claiming success — meant work could be acknowledged and then silently lost, and a peer session could even accept a duplicate of a "successful" mutation. Honest success semantics remove that trap: a green result now means the work is on disk.

## What changed

- A small, pure durability gate (`disk-persist.ts`): a typed disk-write outcome plus `DiskProjectionPersistError` that carries explicit "may be durable in Temporal — do not blind-retry" semantics.
- The projection writer is now awaited and classified. Durability-critical mutations gate success on a confirmed disk write; if it fails they surface the typed error instead of swallowing it.
- Non-critical cache-refresh paths keep their fast best-effort behavior — explicitly, at the call site — so hot paths aren't taxed.

## What was verified

- New tests: durability-gate unit test, spec-delta failure-propagation test, and a task-mutation durability test (all green).
- No regressions: full project check (types, lint, format, schemas, manifests, isolation) green; a 1344-test sweep across storage + Temporal passed.
- Guardrails held: the orphaned-workflow safety guard (SC4) and the disk-first read path are untouched — verified live this session, where disk reads returned in 40ms while the workflow was fully wedged.

## Risks & follow-ups

- **Scoped-out by design (Epic entry 6):** concurrent-session projection serialization — two known races (a peer reseeding from stale disk mid-mutation; a stale whole-file overwrite) where the disk projection can still regress under simultaneous sessions. A robust fix needs a monotonic generation/lease the change state doesn't yet carry; adding it touches the replay-sensitive reducer that has repeatedly poisoned this Epic, so it was deliberately deferred (captured in wisdom `ws-V_e5tl`). This change delivers single-writer honesty, not concurrent-writer durability.
- No power-loss/`fsync` durability (out of scope; the failure mode addressed is process/session exit, which the OS page cache survives).

## Provenance

Defect-origin change in Epic `hardenTemporalReliability` (entry 14). Direction and the SC4-constraint reading were user-approved; an independent design validator raised the concurrency-scope CONFLICT, resolved by explicit user decision to defer it to entry 6.
